chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad al-Za'farani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever seeks trade becomes independent of people. I said, 'And even if he is the breadwinner?' He said, 'And even if he is the breadwinner. Indeed, nine-tenths of livelihood are in trade.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical benefit of engaging in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates trade as a primary means of securing rizq, asserting that nine-tenths of sustenance resides within it. He clarifies that this financial independence applies even to the sole breadwinner, validating commerce as a dignified and essential vocation rather than merely a supplementary activity. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the permissibility and virtue of lawful economic engagement as a form of self-sufficiency and social contribution.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Al Za’afrany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who seeks the business becomes needless from the people’.
I said, ‘And even if he was the (only) breadwinner?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And even if he was the (only) breadwinner. None-tenths of the livelihood is in the business’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad al- Za’faraniy from who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who seeks business becomes independent of people.’ I then asked, ‘Even if he has dependents?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, even if he has dependents; nine-tenth of sustenance is in business.’”
